newsitem.title: UK: POLL-Consumer confidence rises in August - GfK.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Consumer confidence rises in August - GfK.

text.p: British consumer confidence improved in August, with a record number of consumers reporting the month was a good time to spend cash on big items, a survey said on Tuesday.

The monthly European Commission/GfK survey's composite consumer confidence balance rose to +8 in August, from +7 in July on a weighted basis, while its major purchases measure made a new monthly high of +19 in August compared with +17 in July.
The survey found 40 percent of consumers said now was a good time to make a major purchase compared with 38 percent in July and 32 percent in June.
The percentage of consumers who said it was not a good time to make a major purchase was steady at 21 percent, unchanged since May.

The household finances balance covering the last year rose to +4 in August from +1 in July, while the forward looking index, which measures expectations for households finances over the next 12 months stayed steady at +5.

The outlook on the economy improved slightly too in August. The economic situation balance rose to +6 in August compared with +1 in July. The index measuring the outlook for the economy over the next year stayed steady at +9.
The weighted prices balance eased to 81.0 from 81.5 in July.

Geoffrey Dicks, UK economist at NatWest Markets, said consumers were clearly growing more confident, thanks in part to windfall cash from converting building societies and competitive pricing in the shops.
"The major purchases index hit another monthly high, a combination of the windfall gains and keen pricing in the high street."
Dicks said with the Bank of England, having signalled interest rates are on hold, there was little to upset the consumers in the months ahead.
Around 2000 consumers were questioned for the survey between August 1 and 14.
